summary: Objective 4 of Wave 35, closed on the harness side, open on the wiring side. Confirmed from a clean-checkout perspective: db008_storage_replay_guard.harness.sh was NOT reproducible. Its manifest.json and 00-bootstrap.sql were never committed and nothing invoked it, so the Wave 33 CP-059 proof was a claim, not evidence. It is now self-contained and runs 10 real scenarios from the tree. What is still missing is a package.json script and a CI job, both outside the database lane's file ownership.
completed: VERIFIED THE FIXTURES WERE NOT COMMITTED. `git ls-files supabase/tests/ | grep db008_storage` returns exactly four files, none of them manifest.json or 00-bootstrap.sql. The committed bootstrap under a different name, db008_storage_replay_bootstrap.sql, WAS present all along; the harness was looking for 00-bootstrap.sql, which is why the Wave 34 run reported zero scenarios. So the defect was a filename mismatch plus a missing manifest, not a missing fixture.

The harness now creates and destroys its own throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster, generates its own scenario manifest by running db008_storage_replay_extract.mjs into its temp dir, loads the committed fixture, and still asserts its own post-reset state (2 storage tables / 0 policies / owner=supabase_storage_admin / replay role not superuser) before trusting any scenario. It needs nothing but the repository and a local PostgreSQL 16.

A SECOND, WORSE DEFECT WAS FIXED IN THE EXTRACTOR. db008_storage_replay_extract.mjs read the pre-guard text from `git show HEAD:<file>`. That was valid while the CP-059 guard was an uncommitted working-tree edit. It is not valid now: the guard is committed, HEAD equals the working tree, and the comparison silently degrades to guarded-vs-guarded, in which every scenario passes without ever exercising the failure mode the harness exists to prove. The extractor now SYNTHESISES the unguarded form by unwrapping the `do $storage_replay_guard_N$ begin ... exception when others ... end` blocks, which is the pre-guard text derived from the tree itself and stays correct as the migrations change. A block that does not match the expected shape is a hard error, never a silent pass-through.

Result: 10 scenarios, 10 passed, 0 failed, exit 0. 5 of the 10 unguarded forms abort as a non-owner replay role and all 10 guarded forms complete with a sqlstate/sqlerrm warning; the owner-applied policy set is identical to the original in all 10; the form is idempotent over three applies. NOTE the honest delta from Wave 33, which reported all 10 originals aborting: 5 do not, because their inner body carries a pg_policies existence guard that is a no-op on a fresh schema. The synthesized original is not the historical blob, and the report says so.

supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh added: one entry point for all nine database-lane harnesses, each with a one-line statement of what a pass does and does not prove, an explicit list of the four things that need a live target and are therefore never silently claimed, and a hard failure when zero harnesses run. That last rule exists because the Wave 33 harness passed having executed nothing.
next_steps: ORCHESTRATOR: add `"check:database-harnesses": "bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh"` to package.json. It is deliberately not run as part of check:migration-chain: those harnesses create a PostgreSQL cluster and take minutes, and a shared gate that is slow gets skipped.

ORCHESTRATOR / QA: add a CI job on a runner with a PostgreSQL 16 service (services: postgres:16) running the same command. The harnesses locate PostgreSQL at /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@16/bin and SKIP cleanly if it is absent, so on a Linux runner they will skip rather than fail until PGBIN is pointed at the service; wire PGBIN explicitly. A CI job that silently skips is the Wave 33 failure in a new location, so the job should assert that the harnesses RAN, which db008_run_all.sh's `ran N` line makes possible.

RELEASE: these are local emulations. A green run is evidence about the migration chain and nothing about staging or production; the operator's manual apply and the hosted postflight remain the gate (CP-051).
blockers: package.json and .github/workflows/** are outside the database lane's file ownership for this wave, so the wiring is handed over rather than done. This is a handoff, not silent scope expansion.

Every harness needs a local PostgreSQL 16 at /opt/homebrew/opt/postgresql@16/bin (overridable with PGBIN). On a machine without it they print SKIP and exit 0, which is correct for a developer machine and WRONG for CI. The CI job must therefore assert that scenarios ran, not merely that the command exited 0.
verification: git ls-files supabase/tests/ | grep db008_storage -> db008_storage_replay_bootstrap.sql, db008_storage_replay_extract.mjs, db008_storage_replay_guard.harness.sh, db008_storage_replay_guard_contract.sql. No manifest.json, no 00-bootstrap.sql. Confirms the Wave 33 fixture gap.
bash supabase/tests/db008_storage_replay_guard.harness.sh -> 10 passed, 0 failed, exit 0, with the per-scenario rc and warning counts printed.
bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh -> ran 9, skipped 1 (view-delta, which needs a gen-types payload), failed 0.
bash supabase/tests/db008_run_all.sh --list -> lists all nine harnesses and the four live-target commands that are never claimed.
NOT verified: no CI run, no hosted environment, and the harnesses' own PostgreSQL cluster is a Homebrew build, not the PostgreSQL version a Supabase project runs.
